translation_en: Abu Ma‘mar said: ‘Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: It was counted against me as one divorce.

Al-Humaydi narrated to us: Al-Walid narrated to us: Al-Awza‘i narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Zuhri, ‘Which of the Prophet’s wives sought refuge from him?’ He said: ‘Urwah informed me, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that when the daughter of al-Jawn was brought in to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and he approached her, she said, ‘I seek refuge in Allah from you.’ He said to her, ‘You have sought refuge with the Greatest. Go back to your family.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Hajjaj ibn Abi Mani‘ narrated it from his grandfather, from al-Zuhri, that ‘Urwah informed him that ‘A’ishah said this.

Abu Nu‘aym narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghaseel narrated to us, from Hamzah ibn Abi Usayd, from Abu Usayd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We went out with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, until we came to a garden called al-Shawt, between two gardens. The Prophet said, ‘Sit here.’ He went in. The Jawniyyah had been brought, and she was placed in a house among the palm trees, in the home of Umaymah bint al-Nu‘man ibn Sharahil, with her nurse who had cared for her. When the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, entered upon her, he said, ‘Give yourself to me.’ She said, ‘Would a queen give herself to a commoner?’ He reached out his hand to touch her and calm her, but she said, ‘I seek refuge in Allah from you.’ He said, ‘You have sought refuge with One who grants refuge.’ Then he came out to us and said, ‘Abu Usayd, give her two garments of Raziqi cloth and send her back to her family.’

Al-Husayn ibn al-Walid al-Naysaburi said, from ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Abbas ibn Sahl, from his father and Abu Usayd, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, married Umaymah bint Sharahil. When she was brought in to him, he extended his hand toward her, but she seemed to dislike that. So he ordered Abu Usayd to prepare her for departure and give her two garments of Raziqi cloth.

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Wazir narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Hamzah, from his father, and from ‘Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa‘d, from his father, with this same report.

Hajjaj ibn Minhāl narrated to us: Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Ghallab, Yunus ibn Jubayr, who said: I asked Ibn ‘Umar, ‘A man divorced his wife while she was menstruating.’ He said, ‘Do you know Ibn ‘Umar? Ibn ‘Umar divorced his wife while she was menstruating, and ‘Umar went to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and told him about it. He ordered him to take her back. When she becomes pure, if he wants to divorce her, let him divorce her.’ I asked, ‘Did he count that as a divorce?’ He said, ‘What do you think? If he was incapable and foolish?’

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, that Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi informed him that ‘Uwaymir al-‘Ajlani came to ‘Asim ibn ‘Adi al-Ansari and said, ‘‘Asim, what do you think if a man finds another man with his wife? Should he kill him, in which case you would kill him, or what should he do? Ask the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, for me about that.’ ‘Asim asked the Messenger of Allah about it, but the Messenger of Allah disliked questions of that sort and criticized them, until what ‘Asim heard from the Messenger of Allah weighed heavily on him. When ‘Asim returned to his family, ‘Uwaymir came and said, ‘‘Asim, what did the Messenger of Allah say to you?’ ‘Asim said, ‘You have brought me nothing good. The Messenger of Allah disliked the question I asked him.’ ‘Uwaymir said, ‘By Allah, I will not stop until I ask him about it myself.’ He went to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, while he was among the people and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, what do you think if a man finds another man with his wife? Should he kill him, in which case you would kill him, or what should he do?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Allah has revealed concerning you and your wife. Go and bring her here.’ Sahl said: They then invoked curses upon one another, while I was with the people near the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. When they had finished, ‘Uwaymir said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I would be lying about her if I kept her,’ and he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ordered him to do so. Ibn Shihab said: This became the practice for spouses who invoke curses upon one another.

Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to me: ‘Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah told him: The wife of Rifa‘ah al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Rifa‘ah divorced me conclusively. Then I married ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr al-Qurazi, but he has only something like the fringe of a garment.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Perhaps you want to return to Rifa‘ah? No, not until he tastes your sweetness and you taste his.’

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me: Yahya narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who said: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from ‘A’ishah, that a man divorced his wife three times. She married another man, who then divorced her. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was asked, ‘Is she lawful for the first husband?’ He said, ‘No, not until she has tasted his sweetness as the first husband tasted hers.’

‘Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Al-A‘mash narrated to us: Muslim narrated to us, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, gave us a choice, and we chose Allah and His Messenger. He did not count that against us as anything.

Musaddad narrated to us: Yahya narrated to us, from Isma‘il: ‘Amir narrated to us, from Masruq, who said: I asked ‘A’ishah about the choice. She said, ‘The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, gave us a choice.’ I asked, ‘Was that a divorce?’ Masruq said, ‘I would not care if I gave her the choice once or a hundred times, after she has chosen me.’

Al-Layth said, from Nafi‘: When Ibn ‘Umar was asked about someone who had divorced his wife three times, he would say, ‘If you had divorced her once or twice, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, instructed me about what to do. But if you have divorced her three times, she is forbidden to you until she marries another husband.’

Muhammad narrated to us: Abu Mu‘awiyah narrated to us: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah narrated to us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said: A man divorced his wife. She then married another man, who divorced her. He had only something like a fringe, and she had not obtained what she wanted from him. Before long, he divorced her. She came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, my husband divorced me. I married another man, who consummated the marriage with me, but he had only something like a fringe. He came to me only once and did not reach what he wanted from me. Am I now lawful for my first husband?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘You are not lawful for your first husband until the other man has tasted your sweetness and you have tasted his.’

Al-Hasan ibn Sabbah narrated to me; he heard al-Rabi‘ ibn Nafi‘: Mu‘awiyah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Ya‘la ibn Hakim, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, who informed him that he heard Ibn ‘Abbas say: If a man declares his wife forbidden to him, it is nothing. He said, ‘Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example’ (33:21).

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sabbah narrated to me: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ‘Ata’ claimed that he heard ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Umayr say: I heard ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, say that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, used to stay with Zaynab bint Jahsh and drink honey at her house. Hafsah and I agreed that whichever of us the Prophet entered upon should say to him, “I smell maghafir on you. Have you eaten maghafir?” He went in to one of them, and she said that to him. He said, “No, rather I drank honey at Zaynab bint Jahsh’s house, and I will not do so again.” Then these verses were revealed: “O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you…,” through “If you two repent to Allah…” (66:1–4), concerning ‘A’ishah and Hafsah; and “When the Prophet confided something to one of his wives…” (66:3), concerning his words, “Rather, I drank honey.”

Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra’ narrated to us: ‘Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, loved honey and sweets. When he finished the afternoon prayer, he would visit his wives and draw near to one of them. He went to Hafsah bint ‘Umar and stayed there longer than he usually stayed. I became jealous and asked about it. I was told that a woman from her clan had given her a small leather container of honey, and she had given the Prophet a drink from it. I said, ‘By Allah, we will devise a plan for him.’ I said to Sawdah bint Zam‘ah, ‘He will come near you. When he does, say, “Have you eaten maghafir?” He will say no. Then say to him, “What is this smell I notice from you?” He will tell you, “Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.” Then say, “The bees must have fed on ‘urfut.” I will say the same, and you, Safiyyah, say it too.’ Sawdah said: By Allah, as soon as he stood at the door, I was about to say what you had told me, for fear of you. When he came near her, Sawdah said, ‘Messenger of Allah, have you eaten maghafir?’ He said, ‘No.’ She said, ‘Then what is this smell I notice from you?’ He said, ‘Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.’ She said, ‘The bees must have fed on ‘urfut.’ When he came around to me, I said something similar. When he came around to Safiyyah, she said the same. When he came around to Hafsah, she said, ‘Messenger of Allah, shall I give you some of it to drink?’ He said, ‘I have no need of it.’ Sawdah said, ‘By Allah, we have deprived him of it.’ I told her, ‘Be quiet.’

Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘Allah has pardoned my community for what their selves think, so long as they do not act upon it or speak of it.’ Qatadah said: If he divorces in his own mind, it is nothing.

Asbagh narrated to us: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Salamah informed me, from Jabir, that a man from Aslam came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, while he was in the mosque and said that he had committed adultery. The Prophet turned away from him, so he moved to the side toward which the Prophet had turned away and testified against himself four times. The Prophet called him and said, ‘Are you insane? Have you been married?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ The Prophet ordered that he be stoned at the prayer ground. When the stones hurt him, he ran until he was caught at al-Harrah and killed.

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman and Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: A man from Aslam came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, while he was in the mosque. He called out, ‘Messenger of Allah, the other man has committed adultery’—meaning himself. The Prophet turned away from him, so he moved to the side toward which the Prophet had turned away and said it again. The Prophet turned away from him, so he moved to that side and said it again. The Prophet turned away from him, so he moved to that side. On the fourth time, after he had testified against himself four times, the Prophet called him and asked, ‘Are you insane?’ He said, ‘No.’ The Prophet said, ‘Take him and stone him.’ He had been married. Al-Zuhri also said: Someone who heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Ansari informed me that he was among those who stoned him. They stoned him at the prayer ground in Madinah. When the stones hurt him, he ran until they caught him at al-Harrah, and they stoned him until he died.

Azhar ibn Jamil narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us: Khalid narrated to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas: The wife of Thabit ibn Qays came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I have no complaint against Thabit ibn Qays concerning his character or religion, but I dislike falling into disbelief in Islam.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Will you return his garden to him?’ She said, ‘Yes.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Accept the garden, and divorce her once.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah said: This report is not supported through Ibn ‘Abbas.

Ishaq al-Wasiti narrated to us: Khalid narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha’, from ‘Ikrimah, that the sister of ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy reported this same account. She said, ‘Will you return his garden to him?’ She said, ‘Yes.’ She returned it to him, and the Prophet ordered him to divorce her. Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated from Khalid, from ‘Ikrimah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, with the wording, ‘And divorce her.’

Ibn Abi Tamimah narrated it, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The wife of Thabit ibn Qays came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I have no complaint against Thabit concerning his religion or his character, but I cannot bear him.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Will you return his garden to him?’ She said, ‘Yes.’

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Mukharrimi narrated to us: Qirad Abu Nuh narrated to us: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The wife of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shimas came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I have no complaint against Thabit concerning his religion or character, but I fear falling into disbelief.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Will you return his garden to him?’ She said, ‘Yes.’ She returned it to him, and he ordered Thabit to separate from her.
Sulayman narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, from ‘Ikrimah, that it was Jamilah. Then he mentioned the hadith.

Abu al-Walid narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say, ‘The Banu al-Mughirah have asked my permission for ‘Ali to marry their daughter. I will not give permission.’

Isma‘il ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Rabi‘ah ibn Abi ‘Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: There were three precedents in the case of Barirah. One was that when she was freed, she was given the choice concerning her husband. The Messenger of Allah said, ‘The right of wala’ belongs to the one who frees the slave.’ The Messenger of Allah came in while a cooking pot was boiling with meat. Bread and some household relish were brought to him. He said, ‘Did I not see a pot with meat in it?’ They said, ‘Yes, but that meat was given as charity to Barirah, and you do not eat charity.’ He said, ‘For her it is charity, and for us it is a gift.’
Abu al-Walid narrated to us: Shu‘bah and Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: I saw him as a slave—meaning Barirah’s husband.

‘Abd al-A‘la ibn Hammad narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: That was Mughith, a slave of so-and-so—meaning Barirah’s husband. I can almost see him following her through the streets of Madinah, weeping for her.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Ayyub, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Barirah’s husband was a black slave called Mughith, a slave of Banu So-and-so. I can almost see him going around behind her through the streets of Madinah.

Muhammad narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab informed us: Khalid narrated to us, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, that Barirah’s husband was a slave called Mughith. I can almost see him following her behind, weeping, with tears running down his beard. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to al-‘Abbas, ‘‘Abbas, are you not amazed at Mughith’s love for Barirah and Barirah’s aversion to Mughith?’ The Prophet said, ‘If only you would take him back.’ She said, ‘Messenger of Allah, are you commanding me?’ He said, ‘I am only interceding.’ She said, ‘I have no need of him.’
